title: The Ice-Locked Planet That Birthed Complex Life: Hard Snowball Earth vs. Slushball, Jormungand & the Cryogenian Rise of Algae — From Harland's 1964 tropical tillites, Budyko's 1969 runaway ice-albedo equations, and Kirschvink's 1992 Snowball coinage to Hoffman & Schrag's (1998) Namibia cap-carbonate synthesis, Hoffman et al.'s (2017) dynamic sea-glacier & cryoconite refinement, Brocks et al.'s (2017) post-Sturtian Rise of Algae sterane explosion, Hyde & Peltier's (2000) Slushball open-ocean GCM, Allen & Etienne's (2008) wave-rippled sedimentary challenge, Abbot, Voigt & Koll's (2011) bare-sea-ice Jormungand attractor (+64 W/m^2 albedo jump), and two worked calculations on 350 PAL volcanic escape clocks, 1.17-km sea-glacier light cutoffs, 40-sigma Delta-17O barometry & paleomagnetic Fisher bounds

teenKit.tldr: About 700 million years ago, Earth's ice sheets advanced all the way to the equator, plunging the planet into a deep freeze before a sudden volcanic greenhouse gas buildup melted it back into a steaming tropical paradise.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how Earth survived global extreme climate whiplash gives us a baseline for how planetary climate systems can radically flip—and how life manages to bounce back from near-total extinction.
keyTakeaways: Glacial debris found in tropical Namibia proves that ice sheets once floated near the equator, defying intuitive climate expectations.
The 'ice-albedo' feedback loop can become a runaway trap: white ice reflects sunlight, cooling the planet further until the entire ocean freezes over.
Massive volcanic eruptions eventually pumped enough CO2 through the ice armor to trigger a hyper-greenhouse, setting the stage for complex life to evolve.

A distinct layer of limestone sitting directly on top of glacial deposits that forms in hot, tropical ocean waters.
A climate cycle where expanding ice reflects more sunlight, causing even more cooling and ice growth.
A rival theory to Snowball Earth proposing that the equator remained a band of open, slushy ocean water rather than freezing solid.

quiz.question: What geologic evidence in Namibia stunned scientists by pointing to equatorial glaciers?
options: Volcanic ash mixed with dinosaur fossils
Jagged glacial boulders sitting right beneath hot-water limestone
Deep sea trenches filled with modern plastic
Radioactive uranium deposits in dry riverbeds
quiz.explanation: Glacial rubble resting directly beneath tropical cap carbonates indicates a violent shift from deep freeze to extreme heat.

quiz.question: What primary mechanism finally broke Earth out of its extreme global ice-locked state?
options: A massive asteroid impact that shattered the ice sheet
Volcanic eruptions pumping greenhouse gases like CO2 through the ice
Intense solar flares heating up the upper atmosphere
Giant marine animals melting the ice with body heat
quiz.explanation: Volcanoes kept erupting beneath and through the ice, eventually accumulating enough CO2 to trap heat and trigger a super-greenhouse.

quiz.question: What is the core argument of the 'Slushball Earth' rival hypothesis?
options: The ice sheets never left the polar regions
The planet was entirely melted with no ice at all
A narrow band of open, slushy ocean survived near the equator
The ice was made of methane slush instead of water
quiz.explanation: Climate models like Hyde & Peltier's suggested that open-water physics at the equator prevented total global freezing.
